text:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing weird canary exposure skew when a canary is region-scoped + the router falls back to a low-cost variant. Canary doesn't seem to register in metrics. Anyone seen this?
ton y: yep, saw it on staging earlier today — EU traffic that should be in the canary ended up on the quantized variant and the canary dashboard showed 0 hits.
li: quick summary of current flow: route by customer.tier -> preferred model -> region placement. If model placement fails: fallback chain is smaller-quantized variant -> cross-region attempt -> queue. Canary exposure is currently applied at the tier matching stage, not at the final served variant.
eva: that ordering seems wrong — if canary assignment is done before placement but after region decisions we can lose fidelity when we cross-region/fallback.
maria: exactly. Proposed: evaluate canary gating as the final decision before any fallback that changes the variant or region. If a request is sampled into canary, it must either serve the canary model or explicitly be marked as "canary_dropped" and routed to stable, not quietly served by a different variant.
dan: +1. For A/B experiments where B is a cheaper variant, we should avoid silently substituting B for latency/cost reasons — that'll mask regressions. There needs to be an explicit fallback policy per experiment: preserve|failover_to_stable|drop.
tony: agreed. Temporary mitigation idea: make fallback behavior tier-aware. For canary cohort set cross-region fallback to disabled; either failover to stable in-region or return 503 so we can surface the issue.
li: example config proposal (staging):
```
routing:
  - match: customer.tier == "enterprise"
    canary:
      id: "exp-a-2026-03"
      pct: 5
      scope: "region"    # options: global | region | tier
      failthrough: "preserve" # preserve | stable | drop
```
eva: :thumbsup: we also need telemetry changes. Tag every request with canary_id, initial_candidate (true/false), final_variant, and a flag canary_fidelity_reason (e.g., fallback_capacity, cross_region, quota). Dashboard should surface 'lost_canary_due_to_fallback' and 'canary_fidelity_pct'.
dan: quota interplay note: reserved capacity for enterprise should be considered. If canary placement hits a reserved pool, fallback behavior must not consume shared capacity in a way that affects other customers.
maria: UX note for Console: add a checkbox "Preserve canary variants across fallbacks" with a tooltip: "If enabled, requests sampled into the canary will not be silently rerouted to cheaper variants or other regions — they will either be served by the canary or routed to stable/fail as configured."
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary-config-service v2 deployed to staging (build #3421) :rocket:
tony: I'll implement the short-term mitigation (disable cross-region fallbacks for canary cohort) and add a temporary alert if canary fidelity drops > 5%.
li: I'll open the PR that moves canary-eval to before any variant-changing fallback and add the telemetry tags + dashboard tile: 'canary_fidelity' = canary_served_count / canary_candidate_count. Alert if < 95%.
eva: also add to rollout docs: explicit contract for A/B experiments about what to do when preferred variant is unavailable. Add the failthrough options and examples.
maria: action items: li (PR to gating-before-fallback + telemetry), tony (mitigation + alert), eva (console copy + docs + dashboard tile). Ping me when PRs are up. Thanks everyone :pray:
li: will do, aiming for PR today.
dan: cool — I'll audit existing canaries for fidelity regressions and post a short report.
maria: perfect. If anything unexpected shows up, please @maria in the thread so we can pause the rollout.
